qa.question: Should the owner be Forest Junction Energy Center LLC instead of Invenergy LLC?
qa.finding: The application says Forest Junction Energy Center LLC is a subsidiary of Invenergy Thermal Development Holdings LLC. The database shows Invenergy LLC at 100 percent.
qa.recommendation: Change the owner on all five units to Forest Junction Energy Center LLC [100%] if the reviewer agrees that the project company is the holder. Leave it as is if Invenergy LLC is the entity the tracker uses for Invenergy projects.
qa.note: Open https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=617707 and go to PDF page 14. The first paragraph of the application says the two applicants are 'subsidiaries of Invenergy Thermal Development Holdings LLC'. Page 14 also says the project company's affiliate signed a procurement agreement with Wisconsin Electric Power Company, but no sale of the plant is announced. qa.question: Is MISO queue entry J4014 at 650 MW part of Union Depot rather than Forest Junction?
qa.finding: The application says J4014 at 650 MW is the Union Depot queue position at the Forest Junction Substation. Forest Junction itself has a signed interconnection agreement for 1,203 MW.
qa.recommendation: Match J4014 to Union Depot and do not count it against the five Forest Junction units. Leave Forest Junction at five units of 240.6 MW.
qa.note: Open https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=617707 and go to PDF page 18. It says 'Forest Junction has signed a Generator Interconnection Agreement with ATC and MISO for 1,203 MW' and 'Union Depot filed a MISO generator interconnection queue position (J4014)' for 650 MW. A second Union Depot entry, J4249 at 100 MW, is also named there. Union Depot Energy Center is its own plant record in this Wisconsin batch, so J4014 belongs there.
